facts.content: Patient presents with acute upper lip swelling and shortness of breath after consuming prawn soup.
facts.source_text: CC: Acute upper lip swelling and SOB after prawn soup

facts.content: The symptoms began approximately 30 minutes after ingestion, starting at the left corner of the upper lip with a progressive pumping sensation.
facts.source_text: Onset ~30 min post ingestion (~1900); started at L corner upper lip; progressive “pumping” sensation

facts.content: Associations include dizziness and possible chest tightness.
Patient had a similar episode approximately one year ago after consuming late-night Chinese or curry, resulting in swelling and breathing difficulty.
facts.source_text: Hx similar episode ~1 yr ago after late-night Chinese/curry → swelling + breathing difficulty

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient regularly uses a Salbutamol inhaler and does not use a brown inhaler.
facts.source_text: Meds: Salbutamol inhaler (regular); no brown inhaler

facts.content: Patient had a severe peanut reaction in childhood requiring hospital treatment and an injection.
facts.source_text: Allx: Peanut (severe reaction in childhood requiring hospital + injection per mother)

facts.content: Prawn or shellfish is the suspected trigger for today's reaction.

Suspected anaphylaxis secondary to prawn or shellfish exposure, presenting with acute lip angioedema, shortness of breath, possible chest tightness, and dizziness, approximately 30 minutes after ingestion.
facts.source_text: Suspected anaphylaxis 2° to prawn/shellfish exposure: acute lip angioedema + SOB +/- chest tightness, dizziness, onset ~30 min post ingestion

facts.content: Patient has a history of peanut anaphylaxis and asthma as a comorbidity.
Emergency services were called for immediate emergency department transfer due to suspected anaphylaxis.
facts.source_text: 999 called; immediate ED transfer for suspected anaphylaxis

facts.content: Patient advised to take any available antihistamine while waiting for the ambulance.
facts.source_text: Take available antihistamine while awaiting ambulance

facts.content: Patient advised to stay with a companion until emergency medical services arrive.
facts.source_text: Stay with companion until EMS arrival

facts.content: Post-hospital follow-up to arrange an epinephrine auto-injector and further allergy management.
facts.source_text: Post-hospital: follow up with clinic to arrange epinephrine auto-injector and further allergy management
